title: Canonical origin composition equals the open-adjoint tower formula, assuming invertible restriction
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $h:U\to V$ and $f:V\to W$ be separated finite-type morphisms of Noetherian schemes. Supply compactifications $d=(i:V\hookrightarrow\overline V,q:\overline V\to W)$ of $f$ and $e=(a:U\hookrightarrow\overline U,p:\overline U\to\overline V)$ of $h i$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Put $H=\overline U\times_{\overline V}V$, $b:H\hookrightarrow\overline U$, $r:H\to V$ and the induced $j:U\hookrightarrow H$. Assume $\overline V,\overline U,H$ are Noetherian. Use the actual ordinary constant-$\Lambda$ pro-etale derived functors $P_t=Rt_{p,*}$, $J_v=v_{p,!}$, the unit-square-counit exchange, the inverse-open-unit map $\lambda_N:i_p^*P_pJ_bN\to P_rN$, its open adjunct $\gamma_N:J_iP_rN\to P_pJ_bN$, and the adjunction open compositor $E_{b,j}:J_bJ_j\simeq J_a$ of [def-trf-proetale-composition-tower-data]. For $L\in D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ put $M=\nu_U^*L$ and $N=J_jM$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Given that $\lambda_N$ is invertible, the independently specified canonical origin composition, conjugated to these three compactification candidates, satisfies
$$\operatorname{towerOriginComposition}(L)=P_q(\gamma_N)\,;\,(\operatorname{finiteDirectImageComposition}_{p,q}^{-1})_{J_bN}\,;\,P_{pq}(E_{b,j,M}).$$
Here semicolons denote composition in the displayed order. This asserts only equality for the specified canonical origin map; it asserts neither invertibility of $\lambda$ nor invertibility of $\gamma$ on any witnessed input.

proof.text: For N=J_j nu^*L choose the explicit bounded-below etale witness j_!L using properOpenSiteExtensionIso. Identify the transported proper/open site mate with towerGamma by identifying the exchanged restriction and open unit, then applying injectivity of the open adjunction Hom equivalence. This identifies the maps; it does not infer invertibility of an adjunct.

Restrict the proper derived compositor through bounded-below inclusion: right-derived composition compatibility gives finiteDirectImageComposition.inv. The open compositor is identified by uniqueness of left adjoints with the canonical composite restriction. Insert e.restrict_i_fst. Apply the finite-site tower paste to obtain exactly the three arrows in the conclusion in bounded-below site coordinates.

Expand towerOriginComposition and evaluate all candidate comparisons through the fully faithful etale-origin equivalence. Each becomes compactSupportSiteComparison, followed by etale compactification comparison, followed by inverse compactSupportSiteComparison. Naturality and transitivity move and cancel the internal comparisons. The composition_site_square equation identifies the result with the bounded-below site compositor of the preceding step, proving the required equality for this canonical map.
